library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Alli_2023_cefazolin")()$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Alli_2023_cefazolin")()$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0291425>

Alli and colleagues measured total and unbound plasma cefazolin in adults
receiving 2 g cefazolin prophylaxis for elective cardiac valve replacement on
cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), fitted a joint total/unbound population PK model
in Pmetrics (NPAG), and used it to estimate the probability of target
attainment (PTA) of 100% fT>MIC over the first 4 hours of surgery.

The structure (Figure 2 of the paper) has three compartments:

1. a **central ("dosing") compartment** of volume Vc whose concentration is the
   **total** plasma cefazolin; clearance acts here and is scaled by serum
   creatinine, `CL = TVCL * (90 / SeCr)`;
2. a **peripheral compartment** exchanging with central through kcp / kpc;
3. an **unbound-drug compartment** of volume Vt whose concentration is the
   **unbound** plasma cefazolin. Drug moves into it from central at rate kct and
   returns at the albumin-scaled protein-binding rate constant
   `PB = (ktc * Bmax + NS) * (ALB / 40)`.

# Population

Sixteen adults (8 women, 8 men; age 18-59 years, mean 44; weight 51-97 kg, mean
75.1) undergoing CPB for elective valve replacement at Charlotte Maxeke
Johannesburg Academic Hospital, South Africa (Table 1 of the paper). Mean serum
creatinine was 76.7 umol/L (range 42-102), mean serum albumin 41.6 g/L (range
33-47) and mean CPB duration 165 min. Each patient received 2 g cefazolin IV 30
minutes before incision, re-dosed with 2 g at 4 hours if surgery was ongoing.
The analysis used 195 total and 64 unbound concentrations.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Alli_2023_cefazolin")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at SeCr 90 umol/L) | log(3.23) L/h | Table 2, Cl mean (CV 36.06%) |
| `lvc` (Vc, total) | log(3.38) L | Table 2, Vc mean (CV 21.59%) |
| `lvp2` (Vt, unbound compartment) | log(6.08) L | Table 2, Vt mean (CV 33.42%) |
| `lk12` (kcp) | log(5.92) 1/h | Table 2, kcp mean (CV 65.58%) |
| `lk21` (kpc) | log(2.24) 1/h | Table 2, kpc mean (CV 51.81%) |
| `lk13` (kct) | log(144.27) 1/h | Table 2, kct mean (CV 10.17%) |
| `lk31` (ktc) | log(195.91) 1/h | Table 2, ktc mean (CV 12.94%) |
| `lbmax` (Bmax) | log(1.01) g/L | Table 2, Bmax mean (CV 45.23%) |
| `lkns` (NS) | log(15.14) | Table 2, NS mean (CV 24.79%) |
| IIV (`eta*`) | omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1) | Table 2, CV% column |
| `addSd`, `propSd` (total) | 1.0 mg/L, 0.1 | Results, assay error C0 and C1 for plasma data |
| `addSd_Cu`, `propSd_Cu` (unbound) | 0.1 mg/L, 0.1 | Results, assay error C0 and C1 for unbound data |
| `cl = TVCL * (90 / CREAT)` | n/a | Results, 'The final clearance model' |
| `kpb = (k31 * bmax + kns) * (ALB / 40)` | n/a | Results, 'The protein binding was described as follows' |
| Three-compartment ODE structure | n/a | Results text and Figure 2 |
| `Cc = central / vc`, `Cu = peripheral2 / vp2` | n/a | Figure 2 volumes; Results (Vc central volume, Vt volume of the unbound compartment) |

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws serum creatinine and
albumin from normal distributions with the Table 1 means and SDs, truncated to
the observed ranges. Subjects receive 2 g over 1 minute (Figure 2: '1 min bolus
intravenous infusion') at 0 and 4 hours and are sampled at the paper's
schedule (2-300 minutes).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20230920)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230920)

n_sub <- 200
rtnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
}
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  CREAT = rtnorm(n_sub, 76.7, 18.6, 42, 102),
  ALB = rtnorm(n_sub, 41.6, 4.57, 33, 47)
)

# Paper sampling schedule (minutes after the first dose), converted to hours.
obs_min <- c(0, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240, 270, 300)

# Builds a dosing + observation event table. Doses are 1-minute infusions into
# `central`; observation rows carry dvid = 1 because the model declares two
# endpoints (Cc, Cu) -- both come back as columns on every observation row.
make_events <- function(cov, dose_times, dose_amts, obs_times) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, k = seq_along(dose_times)) |>
    mutate(time = dose_times[k], amt = dose_amts[k], rate = amt * 60,
           evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_) |>
    select(-k)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- make_events(cohort, c(0, 4), c(2000, 2000), obs_min / 60)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Alli_2023_cefazolin")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))

# Typical patient at the cohort-mean covariates.
typ_events <- make_events(tibble(id = 1L, CREAT = 76.7, ALB = 41.6),
                          c(0, 4), c(2000, 2000), obs_min / 60)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events,
                           returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1 -- mean total and unbound concentrations

Figure 1 of the paper plots the observed mean (SD) total and unbound
concentrations at each sampling time. The means below were read from that
figure by the maintainers (approximately +/- 5 mg/L).

```{r fig1-data}
fig1 <- tibble(
  minute = obs_min[-1],
  total_obs = c(317, 260, 210, 159, 112, 80, 72, 66, 61, 56, 50, 169, 138),
  unbound_obs = c(145, 119, 97, 73, 52, 38, 35, 32, 29, 27, 24, 78, 64)
)

typ_cmp <- sim_typ |>
  mutate(minute = round(time * 60)) |>
  filter(minute > 0) |>
  select(minute, total_typ = Cc, unbound_typ = Cu) |>
  left_join(fig1, by = "minute") |>
  mutate(
    total_pct = 100 * (total_typ - total_obs) / total_obs,
    unbound_pct = 100 * (unbound_typ - unbound_obs) / unbound_obs
  )

typ_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Minute" = minute,
    "Total, typical (mg/L)" = total_typ,
    "Total, Fig 1 mean (mg/L)" = total_obs,
    "Total diff (%)" = total_pct,
    "Unbound, typical (mg/L)" = unbound_typ,
    "Unbound, Fig 1 mean (mg/L)" = unbound_obs,
    "Unbound diff (%)" = unbound_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-patient prediction (SeCr 76.7 umol/L, ALB 41.6 g/L) against the Figure 1 observed means.")
```

```{r fig1-gate}
# Deterministic (typical-value) comparison, so a tight bound is safe. The total
# concentration is the primary endpoint (195 samples) and the model reproduces
# its mean profile: a mis-transcribed CL, Vc or binding constant moves the whole
# profile by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(typ_cmp$total_pct)) < 10)
# Unbound fraction implied by the binding structure at the typical covariates.
# The model's Cu / Cc settles near 0.36; the observed means in Figure 1 sit
# nearer 0.45-0.5 (see Assumptions and deviations).
fu_typ <- with(sim_typ[sim_typ$time > 1, ], median(Cu / Cc))
stopifnot(fu_typ > 0.3, fu_typ < 0.45)
fu_typ
```

```{r fig1-plot}
# Replicates Figure 1 of Alli 2023 (observed means) with a VPC overlay.
vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, time, Total = Cc, Unbound = Cu) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Total, Unbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(time, analyte) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(conc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95), mean = mean(conc), .groups = "drop"
  )
obs_long <- fig1 |>
  pivot_longer(c(total_obs, unbound_obs), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "total_obs", "Total", "Unbound"),
         time = minute / 60)

ggplot(vpc, aes(time * 60, Q50, colour = analyte, fill = analyte)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs_long, aes(y = conc), shape = 21, size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (min)", y = "Cefazolin (mg/L)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = paste("Lines/ribbons: simulated median and 90% interval (n = 200).",
                       "Points: observed means read from Figure 1 of Alli 2023."))
```

## Figure 3 -- probability of target attainment

The paper's PTA simulations require the **unbound** concentration to exceed the
MIC for 100% of the first 4 hours of surgery, and (Methods) compute the unbound
concentration as a **fixed 26% of the total** -- the 'worst case' unbound
fraction the authors measured at 120 minutes -- rather than from the model's
unbound compartment. The replication below does the same: the target is
`0.26 * Cc >= MIC` at every time point from the end of the first infusion to 4
hours. Doses inside the 4-hour window are those of each regimen (a 4-hourly
regimen contributes only its first dose).

```{r pta-sim}
pta_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(1 / 60, 4, by = 2 / 60), 2 - 1e-3, 4)))
mic_grid <- 2^(-4:6)

pta_scenarios <- tribble(
  ~panel, ~label, ~creat, ~alb, ~t2, ~d1, ~d2,
  "a", "1g4h", 50, 35, NA, 1000, NA,
  "a", "2g4h", 50, 35, NA, 2000, NA,
  "a", "3g4h", 50, 35, NA, 3000, NA,
  "a", "1g2h", 50, 35, 2, 1000, 1000,
  "a", "2g2h", 50, 35, 2, 2000, 2000,
  "a", "2g/1g 2h", 50, 35, 2, 2000, 1000,
  "a", "3g/1.5g 2h", 50, 35, 2, 3000, 1500,
  "b", "Cr50", 50, 35, NA, 2000, NA,
  "b", "Cr75", 75, 35, NA, 2000, NA,
  "b", "Cr100", 100, 35, NA, 2000, NA,
  "c", "Alb30", 75, 30, NA, 3000, NA,
  "c", "Alb35", 75, 35, NA, 3000, NA,
  "c", "Alb40", 75, 40, NA, 3000, NA
) |>
  mutate(scenario = row_number())

pta_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pta_scenarios)), function(i) {
  s <- pta_scenarios[i, ]
  times <- if (is.na(s$t2)) 0 else c(0, s$t2)
  amts <- if (is.na(s$t2)) s$d1 else c(s$d1, s$d2)
  cov <- tibble(id = (i - 1L) * n_sub + seq_len(n_sub),
                CREAT = s$creat, ALB = s$alb, scenario = i)
  make_events(cov, times, amts, pta_grid)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(pta_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

pta_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = pta_events, keep = "scenario",
                           returnType = "data.frame")

trough_free <- pta_sim |>
  filter(time >= 1 / 60) |>
  group_by(scenario, id) |>
  summarise(min_free = min(0.26 * Cc), .groups = "drop")

pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(scenario = pta_scenarios$scenario, mic = mic_grid) |>
  left_join(trough_free, by = "scenario", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(scenario, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = mean(min_free >= mic), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(pta_scenarios |> select(scenario, panel, label), by = "scenario")
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 3a-c of Alli 2023.
panel_titles <- c(a = "(a) regimens, SeCr 50, ALB 35",
                  b = "(b) 2 g 4-hourly, ALB 35",
                  c = "(c) 3 g 4-hourly, SeCr 75")
ggplot(pta, aes(mic, pta, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mic_grid, labels = format(mic_grid, drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2, labeller = labeller(panel = panel_titles)) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (100% fT>MIC, 0-4 h)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Simulated with 0.26 x total concentration as unbound; n = 200 per curve.")
```

The legible curves of Figure 3 were read by the maintainers at the plotted MIC
values (approximately +/- 0.03). The comparison uses the MIC at which PTA
crosses 50% (interpolated on the log2 MIC scale), which is insensitive to which
subjects land in the tails.

```{r pta-compare}
pub_pta <- tribble(
  ~label, ~mic, ~pta_pub,
  "1g4h", 1, 0.95, "1g4h", 2, 0.80, "1g4h", 4, 0.38, "1g4h", 8, 0.04,
  "2g4h", 2, 0.96, "2g4h", 4, 0.80, "2g4h", 8, 0.39, "2g4h", 16, 0.03,
  "3g4h", 4, 0.92, "3g4h", 8, 0.64, "3g4h", 16, 0.20, "3g4h", 32, 0,
  "Cr75", 4, 0.97, "Cr75", 8, 0.79, "Cr75", 16, 0.16, "Cr75", 32, 0,
  "Cr100", 8, 0.95, "Cr100", 16, 0.37, "Cr100", 32, 0, "Cr100", 64, 0,
  "Alb30", 4, 0.92, "Alb30", 8, 0.65, "Alb30", 16, 0.20, "Alb30", 32, 0,
  "Alb35", 4, 0.99, "Alb35", 8, 0.95, "Alb35", 16, 0.55, "Alb35", 32, 0.03,
  "Alb40", 4, 0.99, "Alb40", 8, 0.95, "Alb40", 16, 0.55, "Alb40", 32, 0.03
)

# log2 MIC at which a decreasing PTA curve crosses 0.5.
mic50 <- function(mic, p) {
  o <- order(mic)
  mic <- mic[o]
  p <- p[o]
  i <- which(p >= 0.5 & c(p[-1], 0) < 0.5)[1]
  if (i == length(p)) return(log2(mic[i]))
  log2(mic[i]) + (p[i] - 0.5) / (p[i] - p[i + 1]) * (log2(mic[i + 1]) - log2(mic[i]))
}

sim_mic50 <- pta |>
  filter(label %in% unique(pub_pta$label)) |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(sim = mic50(mic, pta), .groups = "drop")
pub_mic50 <- pub_pta |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(pub = mic50(mic, pta_pub), .groups = "drop")
mic50_cmp <- left_join(pub_mic50, sim_mic50, by = "label") |>
  mutate(diff_dilutions = sim - pub,
         label = factor(label, levels = unique(pub_pta$label))) |>
  arrange(label)

mic50_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(2^x, 2), .names = "{.col}_mgL"),
         diff_dilutions = round(diff_dilutions, 2)) |>
  select(label, pub_mgL, sim_mgL, diff_dilutions) |>
  rename(
    "Curve" = label,
    "MIC50, Figure 3 (mg/L)" = pub_mgL,
    "MIC50, simulated (mg/L)" = sim_mgL,
    "Difference (doubling dilutions)" = diff_dilutions
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "MIC at which PTA crosses 50%: Figure 3 versus simulation.")
```

```{r pta-gate}
# Regimen, renal-function and albumin 35 / 40 g/L curves must land within one
# doubling dilution of the published curve. The albumin 30 g/L curve of
# Figure 3c is a known deviation and is not gated -- see Assumptions and
# deviations.
gated <- mic50_cmp |> filter(label != "Alb30")
stopifnot(
  abs(median(gated$diff_dilutions)) < 0.5,
  all(abs(gated$diff_dilutions) < 1)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. NCA over the first dosing interval (0-4 h) is
computed per analyte on the paper's sampling schedule, so the simulated Cmax is
the 2-minute concentration -- the same quantity as the first plotted point of
Figure 1, which serves as the reference.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(time <= 4) |>
  select(id, time, Total = Cc, Unbound = Cu) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Total, Unbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
# Pre-dose rows are present at time 0 (Cc = 0); guard anyway.
nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> distinct(id, analyte) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, analyte, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(analyte, id, time)

nca_dose <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, time == 0) |>
  select(id, time, amt) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(analyte = c("Total", "Unbound"))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | analyte + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | analyte + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 4, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against published values

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~cmax,
  "Total", 317,
  "Unbound", 145
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "analyte",
  params = "cmax",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median Cmax (2 min) against the Figure 1 observed mean at 2 min. * differs by >20%.")
```

The total Cmax agrees closely. The unbound Cmax is lower than observed, for the
reason given below.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Typical values are the Table 2 means.** Pmetrics NPAG returns a discrete
  non-parametric population distribution, summarised in Table 2 by mean, SD, CV%,
  variance and median. The mean is used as the typical value (it is the figure
  the Results text quotes), and each CV% becomes a log-normal IIV variance,
  omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1), with no covariances. This is a parametric
  approximation of the non-parametric distribution.
- **Residual-error multiplier.** Pmetrics multiplies the assay-error polynomial
  `SD = C0 + C1 * obs` by an estimated noise factor gamma; the paper prints
  C0 and C1 but not gamma. The polynomial is used unscaled (gamma = 1) as a
  `combined1` additive-plus-proportional error.
- **Reading of the binding term.** The Results define
  `PB = (ktc * Bmax + NS) * (ALB / 40)` as 'the rate constant for protein
  binding from unbound to total drug', and Figure 2 draws Bmax and NS acting on
  the unbound-to-central arrow. PB is therefore the rate constant of that
  arrow, replacing ktc there; kct is the central-to-unbound rate constant. Bmax
  is tabulated in g/L and NS without a unit; both are used as dimensionless
  multipliers exactly as the equation is printed. This reading reproduces the
  Figure 1 total profile (median difference `r round(median(typ_cmp$total_pct), 1)`%).
  The alternative (PB as the central-to-unbound constant) was checked by the
  maintainers and fits the total peak markedly worse (about 250 versus 317
  mg/L at 2 minutes).
- **Unbound concentrations are under-predicted.** At the cohort-mean covariates
  the model's unbound-to-total ratio settles at about
  `r round(fu_typ, 2)`, whereas the Figure 1 means imply about 0.45-0.5, so the
  typical unbound profile runs roughly 20-40% below the observed means. The
  paper reports no individual or population predictions for unbound
  concentrations beyond the S1 goodness-of-fit scatter, so the gap cannot be
  traced further; it is not tuned away. Note that the paper itself did not use
  the model's unbound output for its PTA work but a fixed 26% unbound fraction.
- **Covariate references.** The clearance equation normalises SeCr to 90
  umol/L and the binding term normalises albumin to 40 g/L, both described as
  'the population mean value', whereas Table 1 reports means of 76.7 umol/L and
  41.6 g/L. The printed equation values are used.
- **The 30 g/L albumin curve of Figure 3c is not reproduced.** In the model,
  albumin barely moves the total-concentration trough, so with the paper's
  fixed 26% unbound fraction the three albumin curves nearly coincide. The 35
  and 40 g/L curves match Figure 3c, but the published 30 g/L curve sits about
  two-thirds of a doubling dilution to the left. That curve is numerically
  identical to the 3 g 4-hourly curve of Figure 3a (SeCr 50 umol/L), which the
  simulation does reproduce, so the panel may carry a labelling issue. It is
  shown but not gated.
- **Figure 3d (surgery duration) is not replicated.** Its 5- and 6-hour curves
  fall below the 4-hour curve under a 4-hourly regimen, which implies the
  re-dose was not given at 4 hours in those simulations; the timing used is
  not stated.
- **Window of the target.** PTA is evaluated from the end of the first 1-minute
  infusion to 4 hours after the first dose; the paper says 'the first 4 hours
  of surgery' without stating whether the 30-minute pre-incision interval is
  included.
- **Virtual cohort.** Creatinine and albumin are drawn from truncated normals
  with the Table 1 means, SDs and ranges; the paper's covariate distribution is
  otherwise unreported. Fixed covariates (SeCr, ALB) are used for the PTA
  scenarios, as in the paper.
- **Digitised values.** The Figure 1 means and Figure 3 PTA values were read by
  the maintainers from the published figures.
- No correction notice for this article was found on Europe PMC (checked
  2026-10-27).
